task.instruction: Advise the laboratory director who wants trainees to repair a failed containment monitor before tomorrow's study run. Define the repair and learning plan.
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-02] and [doc-04].
Only a certified engineer may return the containment monitor to service; the study cannot run without a validated monitor.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: Supervised trainee repair
documents.content: Two trainees diagnosed a failed power board and propose replacing it tonight using the service manual while the engineer observes remotely.

documents.title: Containment monitor service rule
documents.content: Component replacement and return-to-service testing must be performed and signed by a certified engineer. Observation and non-live practice are permitted.

documents.title: Study run and sample viability
documents.content: Samples remain viable for four days. Delaying tomorrow's run by one day does not invalidate them; a three-day delay does.

documents.title: Certified service options
documents.content: A certified engineer can arrive at 07:00 tomorrow, repair by noon, and let trainees observe. Remote sign-off is not available.

documents.title: Electronics workshop dates
documents.content: The next general electronics workshop is in October and is not a certification course.

target_a.content:
Situation: A nonprofit must prepare monthly donor reports after its analyst leaves.
Shared facts [history-07-01-fact]: A consultant can deliver this month; training two staff takes six weeks; late reports risk a funding delay.
Decision: Use the consultant for one cycle while staff build and document the reporting workflow.
Reasoning: Both choices deliver now but differ in how much current capacity is invested in future ownership.

Situation: A factory needs a machine repair before a large order.
Shared facts [history-07-02-fact]: The vendor can repair in three days; internal technicians need eight days with supervision; the order allows five days of slack.
Message excerpt: Use a joint vendor repair so technicians learn the diagnostic procedure.

Situation: A research group must clean a dataset for a conference deadline.
Shared facts [history-07-03-fact]: Manual cleaning meets the deadline; building reusable validation takes two extra weeks; future studies use the same fields.
Retrospective: Automate the highest-risk checks now and manually finish the remainder.

Situation: A support team is handling a temporary surge in a new product area.
Shared facts [history-07-04-fact]: Specialists can clear the queue quickly; generalists need coached cases; the surge is expected to last two months.
log.decision=Pair specialists with generalists on a protected share of cases.

Situation: A community media group must subtitle a film series.
Shared facts [history-07-05-fact]: An agency can finish every film; volunteer training would finish half and create an ongoing local team.
Decision: Assign half to the agency and use the other half as supervised volunteer production.

Situation: An emergency shelter must restore heat during freezing weather.
Shared facts [history-07-06-fact]: Only a certified contractor can safely restore the failed system before nightfall.
Message excerpt: Hire the certified contractor immediately and document the repair afterward.

Situation: A legal filing is due today and requires licensed counsel.
Shared facts [history-07-07-fact]: Missing the deadline irreversibly forfeits the claim; internal training cannot satisfy representation rules.
Retrospective: Use licensed counsel for the filing and preserve the submitted record.

Situation: A library is migrating a catalog before vendor support ends.
Shared facts [history-07-08-fact]: The vendor offers a turnkey migration; staff-led mapping takes longer but determines future data quality; the deadline allows one rehearsal.
log.decision=Use the rehearsal as a staff-led mapping exercise with vendor backup.
